ref11.title: MLE-bench: Evaluating Machine Learning Agents on Machine Learning Engineering
ref11.significance: MLE-bench uses competition-style problems to test the steps involved in completing a machine-learning task.
ref11.connection: The revised benchmark retains some earlier tasks and swaps others. Comparisons across versions need to account for that change.

ref17.raw: HealthBench Professional: Evaluating Large Language Models on Real Clinician Chats
ref17.title: HealthBench Professional: Evaluating Large Language Models on Real Clinician Chats
ref17.significance: HealthBench Professional evaluates assistance with expert clinical tasks using scoring criteria developed with clinicians.
ref17.connection: The system card uses this benchmark to evaluate assistance on difficult clinical tasks. The grader and task mix help determine what a score measures.

ref18.raw: HealthBench: Evaluating Large Language Models Towards Improved Human Health
ref18.title: HealthBench: Evaluating Large Language Models Towards Improved Human Health
ref18.significance: HealthBench evaluates health-related conversations using explicit criteria for the quality of the response.
ref18.connection: The card explains its move to HealthBench Professional. The earlier test had become less informative for distinguishing recent models.

ref22.raw: Predicting LLM Safety Before Release by Simulating Deployment

ref22.significance: Simulated deployment allows researchers to examine a model’s behavior on a sample of realistic work before wider use.
ref22.connection: The report uses this approach to label model actions on selected work tasks. The frequency of those labels depends on the tasks included.
